title: Protocol for tissue processing and paraffin embedding of mouse brains following ex vivo MRI
protocol: Remove the brain from the skull.
Cut the brain along the midline for sagittal sections using a razor blade.
Cut the brain at notches 4 and 12 for coronal sections.
Place the brain within a brain matrix for slicing.
Store the brain in storage solution at 4°C until required for tissue processing.
Fix tissue using formalin to form cross-linkages with proteins while preserving morphology and antigenicity.
Dehydrate the tissue in a series of alcohols to remove water from the tissue.
Clear the tissue by immersing it in a clearing agent to remove alcohol.
Infiltrate the tissue with paraffin wax.
Rinse the tissue in distilled water twice.
Place each sample inside its own tissue embedding cassette.
Label the cassette with the sample identification.
Dehydrate the tissue in a series of alcohols at 18°C–22°C.
Soak the tissue in 70% ethanol overnight (11 h).
Soak the tissue in 80% ethanol for 45 min.
Soak the tissue in 95% ethanol twice, each time for 45 min.
Soak the tissue in 100% ethanol three times, each time for 15 min.
Soak the tissue in 100% ethanol three times, each time for 30 min.
Clear the tissue in a series of Citroclear at 18°C–22°C.
Soak the tissue in Citroclear for 30 min.
Soak the tissue in Citroclear for 45 min.
Soak the tissue in Citroclear for 60 min.
Infiltrate the tissue with paraffin wax through incubation in a series of molten wax at 60°C.
Soak the tissue in paraffin wax for 30 min.
Soak the tissue in paraffin wax for 45 min.
Soak the tissue in paraffin wax for 60 min.
Warm the paraffin wax in the embedder 30 min prior to use.
Remove tissue embedding cassettes from the tissue processor.
Place tissue embedding cassettes inside the cassette bath of the embedder.
Prepare histology blocks for tissue samples.
Warm forceps to facilitate specimen transfer.
Transfer specimen from cassette to partially filled histology mold using warmed forceps.
Orient specimen into desired position within the mold.
Pour melted paraffin into a histology mold until it is partially filled.
Transfer mold onto cold plate for a few seconds to solidify paraffin and anchor brain.
Use blunt forceps with gentle pressure to avoid damaging the specimen.
Ensure histology mold depth accommodates tissue size and allows at least 1 cm of wax between sample and block edge.
Prepare multi-brain blocks using silicone molds when necessary.
Insert a silicone mold inside a Supa Mega base mold.
Fill the silicone mold with wax.
Keep the mold filled with warm wax in an oven or cassette compartment for 1–6 h.
After allowing the wax to rest, insert a printed guide into the bottom of the mold.
Cover the printed guide with a coverslip covered with double tape.
Transfer the brains into the mold according to the guide.
Record the position of each brain sample.
Use tweezers or a spatula to scratch surfaces occasionally to release bubbles.
Place the labeled cassette on top of the mold.
Return the mold back to the warm plate and fill with melted paraffin up to the upper edge of the cassette.
Transfer the mold to the cold plate and allow the wax to fully solidify for up to 30 minutes.
Separate the mold from the cassette after the wax has solidified.
Remove the coverslip/double tape carefully.
Assess the quality of the block and tissue.
Fill the water bath with distilled water and heat to 42°C.
Chill the block on the surface of ice for <5 min.
Label the slides with the block ID and serial section number.
Remove any excess wax from the outside of the cassette before clamping the block.
Set the paraffin block into the microtome.
Adjust the angle of the blade to 2–5 degrees.
Trim the block at 10–30 μm until a full-faced section is achieved.
Place the block in Mollifex reagent for at least 30 minutes.
Gently wipe away the Mollifex from the block.
Chill the block briefly on the surface of melting ice for up to 5 minutes.
Cut sections using the microtome.
Float the section on a warm water bath until smooth.
Place the section on a glass slide.
Allow the section to dry upright at 18°C–22°C.
Section the block slowly at 4–6 μm with uniform rotation.
Pick up each section using either a small brush or small tweezers.
Discard the first two sections of a ribbon of consecutive sections.
Gently warm breath on the section to prevent rolling and reduce static electricity.
Repeat chilling step if tissue shows signs of drying at edges.
Avoid touching the blade with brush or tweezers to prevent scoring.
Transfer the section onto the water bath and allow it to float until no wrinkles remain (<15 s).
Avoid floating the section for longer to prevent distortion due to expansion.
Collect the section onto a charged glass slide.
Be careful to avoid trapping air bubbles underneath the tissue when transferring.
Dry tissue sections in an upright position overnight at room temperature (18°C–22°C).
Store dried tissue sections in a slide box.
Assess the quality of the sections for absence of wrinkles, folds, scratches, and artefacts.
Ensure the brain remains in its anatomically correct position on the slide.
Avoid positioning the brain close to the edge of the glass slide.
Check for and remove any air bubbles trapped underneath the section.
Ensure sections are free from debris or contamination.
Minimize handling of slides to avoid contaminating them with squamous cells or oils.
Use clean slides and handle them only with gloves.
Unstained slides can be stored in the dark at 18°C–27°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare tissue samples for immunohistochemistry.
Perform antigen retrieval according to the protocol.
Block tissues with blocking solution to reduce nonspecific binding.
Incubate tissues with primary antibody overnight at 4°C.
Wash tissues thoroughly with washing buffer.
Incubate tissues with secondary antibody for specified time.
Wash tissues again with washing buffer.
Visualize antigens using HRP-DAB chromogen.
Counterstain tissue sections with hematoxylin.
Bake the slides for 25 minutes at 60°C.
Deparaffinize and rehydrate the sections using sequential immersion.
Immerse the sections in xylene three times for 5 minutes each.
Submerge and lift the sections 10‒20 times in 100% Industrial denatured alcohol (IDA) twice.
Submerge and lift the sections 10‒20 times in 90% IDA in distilled water.
Submerge and lift the sections 10‒20 times in 70% IDA in distilled water.
Soak the sections in tap water for 2 minutes.
Submerge the slides in 3% H2O2 in PBS in a plastic dish.
Place the submerged slides on an orbital shaker at 18°C–22°C for 30 minutes.
Rinse the slides in water for 1 minute.
Immerse slides in citrate buffer (pH 6) in a plastic staining dish without sealing it.
Heat the buffer and slides in a microwave for 3 minutes on high power (800 W).
Allow the buffer to cool for 5 minutes at room temperature (18°C–22°C).
Reheat in a microwave for 1 minute.
Cool again by letting it sit for 5 minutes at room temperature (18°C–22°C).
Heat once more in a microwave for 1 minute.
Slowly cool the buffer and slides by gently adding water until they are cool.
Do not submerge slides directly into cold water.
Immerse slides in citrate buffer (pH 6) in a plastic staining dish.
Place the staining dish on a metal tray without sealing it.
Run an antigen retrieval program (121°C, 15 psi, 10 min).
Slowly cool the staining dish by gently running water into it until it reaches room temperature.
Coverplate.
Immerse the coverplate into water ensuring there are no bubbles on the surface of the coverplate.
Place the slide on top of the coverplate with the tissue facing the coverplate.
Lift the coverplate/slide out of the water while squeezing slightly to prevent water leaking.
Insert the coverplate with slide into the Shandon Sequenza Rack until it clicks into position.
Mount the glass slide to the coverplates under water.
Remove the coverplate from the water while gently squeezing it.
Slot the coverplate with slide into the Shandon Sequenza Rack until it clicks into position.
Wash with TBS-T for 5 min twice.
Incubate the slides with Protein Block solution at 18°C–22°C for 1 h.
Use 120 μL of Protein Block solution per slide.
Do not wash off the blocking solution after incubation.
Make the primary antibody working solution by diluting the primary antibody in antibody diluent reagent.
Mix well and use fresh before each experiment.
Incubate the slides with the primary antibody for 1 h at 18°C–22°C.
Wash the slides with TBS-T for 5 min twice.
Incubate the slides with the secondary antibody for 1 h at 18°C–22°C.
Use 100 μL per slide.
Wash slides with TBS-T for 5 min twice.
Incubate slides with DAB working solution for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Create a 1:50 dilution of DAB+ chromogen in substrate buffer just before use.
Add 120 μL of the diluted DAB solution per slide.
Quench the DAB with TBS-T for 5 min.
Transfer slides from coverplates to a staining rack underwater to prevent tissue drying.
Counterstain slides in hematoxylin for 1–5 min.
Filter hematoxylin before use.
Blue the slides under running weakly alkaline water for 3–5 min.
Dehydrate and clear slides in sequential staining troughs starting with 70% IDA in distilled water, submerging and lifting 10‒20 times.
Submerge and lift slides 10‒20 times in 90% IDA in distilled water.
Submerge and lift samples 10-20 times in each of the two troughs filled with 100% IDA.
Submerge and lift samples 10-20 times in each of the three troughs filled with xylene.
Remove excess xylene from slides by tapping off excess liquid.
Add 1-3 drops of DPX onto a coverslip.
Place the slide facedown onto the coverslip after removing excess xylene.
Ensure slide and coverslip are well aligned.
Gently apply pressure to remove any air bubbles between the slide and coverslip.
Allow slides to dry overnight in a fume hood at room temperature.
Digitize the stained slides at 40x using a digital slide scanner.
Correct the T2-weighted MRI data for 3D Gibbs-ringing.
Extract the brain from images using an atlas-based segmentation obtained following non-linear registration to a cohort-specific standard space with Pydpiper.
Co-register multi-modal MRI data (T2-weighted, T2∗-weighted and dMRI) using FLIRT.
Run the histology-to-MRI registration pipeline using TIRL.
Register PLP histology to T2-weighted MRI due to their good white and gray matter contrast.
Input the locations of the MRI and histology files into the configuration file (slice_to_volume.json).
Specify the locations of the log files in the configuration file.
Set the image resolutions in the configuration file.
Indicate the slicing plane and direction (coronal, axial or sagittal) in the configuration file.
Provide the approximate location of the slab (center coordinates), as determined from FSLeyes.
Register neighboring histology slides acquired using different stains to the PLP slide.
Run TIRL adjusting the following parameters in the configuration file: Locations of the histology files, locations of the log files, image resolutions.
Assess the quality of the histology-to-histology registration outcome.
Check that images are well aligned and appear anatomically correct.
Verify that edges of tissue and gray/white matter boundaries match between neighboring slides stained for different histological markers.
Ensure images are not distorted.
Use color deconvolution to separate DAB and hematoxylin stains.
Segment DAB specific staining from non-specific staining.
Calculate the SAF map.
Run the optimization pipeline (iterate_alphas.sh).
Adjust the threshold parameter for each stain.
Specify the location of the histology image.
Set the output directory.
Define the starting alpha value.
Determine the alpha increments.
Set the end alpha value for the range.
Specify the segmentation dimension.
Set the patch size.
Locate the logfiles directory.
Examine segmentation images to determine the best threshold without noise and accurately extracting the stain.
Run the default pipeline (default_pipeline.sh).
Adjust the location of the histology image.
Set the output directory.
Define the weighting for segmentation (threshold).
Specify the segmentation dimension.
Set the patch size for high resolution SAF.
Set the patch size for low resolution SAF.
Locate the logfiles directory.
